1  SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988,
 AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:04.01.2014  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:14937  MFA No. 2014 of 2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.397/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, ADDITIONAL MACT, KARKALA.

THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Sri.A.N.Krishna Swamy., learned counsel for the appellant has appeared in person.
2.
Notice to the respondents was ordered on 09.01.2015.
A perusal of the office note depicts that respondent No.1 is served and unrepresented.
A perusal of the daily order sheet depicts that notice to respondent No.2 is held sufficient vide order dated:25.07.2018.
They have neither engaged the services of an advocate nor conducted the case as party in person.
3. The brief facts are these:

On the thirty-first day of January 2011 at about 9:30 am., the claimant was riding his Hero Honda Splendor bearing Registration No.KA-21-K-8893 from Naravi Village of Belthangady Taluk towards Kollur along with his wife Smt.Lalitha as a pillion rider.

When they reached near NC: 2024:KHC:14937 Saligrama Bus Stop of Karkada Village in NH-17, a rider of Hero Honda motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-20-J-7479 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the claimant.
As a result of which, the claimant fell and sustained grievous injuries.

After the accident,
he was shifted to Spandana Maternity and General Hospital, Karkala and admitted as an inpatient from 31.01.2011 to 12.02.2011.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Contending that he is entitled for compensation, the claimant filed claim petition.
In response to the notice, the first respondent remained absent before the Tribunal and hence, he was placed ex-parte.
The second respondent Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement denying the petition averments.
Among other grounds, it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed issues, parties led evidence and marked the documents.
The Tribunal vide Judgment dated:04.01.2014 partly allowed the claim petition and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount.
The Insurance Company has NC: 2024:KHC:14937 assailed the Judgment of the Tribunal in this appeal on several grounds as set-out in the Memorandum of appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has urged several contentions.
Heard, the contentions urged on behalf of the appellant and perused the appeal papers and also the records with utmost care.
5. The point that requires consideration is whether the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability on the Insurance Company.
6. The facts are sufficiently stated and do not require reiteration.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company in presenting his arguments strenuously urged that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Counsel drew the attention of the Court to Section 2(10) and Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and also Ex.R.1 and cross examination of RW1.
Perused the Sections and also the records of the Tribunal with utmost care.

It is pivotal to note that no person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective NC:
2024:KHC:14937 driving license issued to him authorizing him to drive the vehicle.

Needless to say that under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 driving license means the license issued by a competent authority under Chapter-II authorizing the person specified therein to drive, otherwise than as a learner, a motor vehicle or a motor vehicle of any specified class or description.
Ex.R.1 is a true copy of the Driving License of M.V.Nagendranatha - the rider of the offending vehicle.
A perusal of the same reveals that it was issued on 22.02.2011 and it is valid till 19.05.2016.
The rider of the offending vehicle Nagendranatha was examined as RW1.
In the cross examination he admits that he was having only Learner's License as on the date of accident.
Hence, it can be safely concluded that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The Tribunal has overlooked this aspect of the matter and erroneously fastened the liability on the Insurance Company.
This is unsustainable in law.

7. For the reasons stated above, the Judgment dated:04.01.2014 passed by the Court of Senior Civil Judge NC: 2024:KHC:14937 and AMACT, Karkala in MVC No.397/2012 in so far as fastening the liability on the Insurance Company is liable to be set-aside.

sentences.text: Accordingly, it is set-aside.
The Insurance Company is exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation.
8. Resultantly, the Miscellaneous First Appeal is allowed.
The Registry concerned is directed to refund the amount in deposit to the Insurance Company after due identification.
